question: I love Garfiel. What is the background behind the proverbs/sayings he uses? If possible, please tell us sensei's favorite proverb!
answer:
Garfiel spent his time in the Sanctuary reading books, so surprisingly, he's actually quite well-educated. He knows a lot of proverbs and thinks someone who drops a proverb at the right moment looks cool, which leads to him occasionally inventing non-existent proverbs on the fly. He feels that even made-up proverbs sound cool if delivered with good timing. So among what Garfiel says, it's roughly a 7-to-3 ratio—about 30% of them are completely made up.

Among them, my favorite proverbs include "Nobody Can Lift a Quain Stone Alone," which also became an episode subtitle. It worked well and had a great ring to it.

Another favorite is "You cannot run from Reinhard." I love how Reinhard became a living proverb while still alive.

I also like "Reid Astrea draws his sword and laughs before the Dragon," which carries the meaning of "a complete lunatic." I love proverbs that sound cool on the surface but turn out to mean something completely unhinged when you learn the context, so those are my favorites.
